subject.title: Subagent sessions persist after completion, main session becomes unresponsive

question: Should completed run-mode subagent sessions be retained as visible history by default, automatically hidden/archived/deleted, or governed by an explicit retention policy?
rationale: Current code and tests deliberately preserve keep-mode run subagents, but the issue reports that this retained state makes status/session surfaces misleading and can affect parent responsiveness; changing the default is a user-visible session-history contract decision.

options.title: Preserve History, Fix Visibility
options.body: Keep completed child transcripts by default, but make session/task/Control UI/WebChat projections immediately mark them terminal and non-blocking, with cleanup available through explicit actions.

options.title: Auto-Archive Completed Runs
options.body: Archive or hide completed one-shot subagent sessions after terminal cleanup by default, accepting a retention behavior change that needs docs, migration/upgrade proof, and focused UI tests.

options.title: Add Explicit Retention Policy
options.body: Introduce a retention setting only if maintainers decide existing cleanup and doctor/session maintenance surfaces cannot express the desired behavior safely.

recommendation.title: Preserve History, Fix Visibility
recommendation.body: Keep completed child transcripts by default, but make session/task/Control UI/WebChat projections immediately mark them terminal and non-blocking, with cleanup available through explicit actions.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision touches recent session organization, Gateway session-list semantics, and user-visible product behavior where steipete has the strongest current path history.
